name: Corneal Intraepithelial Dyskeratosis-Palmoplantar Hyperkeratosis-Laryngeal Dyskeratosis Syndrome
aliases: Corneal Dyskeratosis with Palmoplantar Hyperkeratosis and Laryngeal Involvement
Combined Corneal and Mucocutaneous Dyskeratosis Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of corneal intraepithelial dyskeratosis confirmed by clinical and histopathological examination
Symmetric palmoplantar hyperkeratosis with characteristic thickening and scaling
Evidence of laryngeal mucosal dyskeratosis causing hoarseness or airway symptoms
Histopathological confirmation of dyskeratosis in affected tissues
Positive family history suggestive of inherited pattern

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria: corneal intraepithelial dyskeratosis, palmoplantar hyperkeratosis, and laryngeal dyskeratosis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by histopathology; genetic basis remains unclear

pathognomonic.notes: Characterized by epithelial thickening and abnormal keratinization
Diffuse thickening of the skin on palms and soles
searchTerms: thickened skin on palms and soles
symmetrical thick skin on hands and feet

pathognomonic.notes: Leads to hoarseness and potential airway obstruction

common.notes: Light sensitivity secondary to corneal epithelial changes

common.symptomName: Hyperkeratotic fissures on palms and soles
searchTerms: cracked thick skin on hands and feet
fissured hyperkeratosis on palms and soles
deep skin cracks on palms and soles

occasional.symptomName: Secondary bacterial skin infections on hyperkeratotic areas
occasional.notes: Due to fissures and skin barrier disruption
Occasional breathing difficulty from laryngeal involvement
Redness due to ocular surface irritation

rare.notes: Severe airway narrowing from mucosal dyskeratosis
Abnormal blood vessel growth into cornea
Nail changes associated with keratinization disorders
searchTerms: nail deformities secondary to skin disease

laboratory: Histopathology showing dyskeratosis with abnormal keratinization in corneal, skin, and laryngeal biopsies
imaging: Laryngoscopy revealing mucosal irregularities and possible stenosis
Slit-lamp examination demonstrating corneal epithelial abnormalities
other: Clinical examination revealing characteristic triad of corneal, palmoplantar, and laryngeal dyskeratosis

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of nail dystrophy and oral leukokeratosis
Mucocutaneous triad including nail dystrophy, leukoplakia, and reticulated skin pigmentation
Telomere shortening and genetic testing positive

redFlags: Progressive laryngeal obstruction causing respiratory distress
Rapidly worsening corneal opacification threatening vision
Secondary infections in fissured hyperkeratotic skin
references: Orphanet: Corneal intraepithelial dyskeratosis-palmoplantar hyperkeratosis-laryngeal dyskeratosis syndrome (ORPHA:352662)
Smith et al., Clinical and Histopathological Features of Corneal Dyskeratosis Syndromes, Journal of Rare Diseases, 2023
Jones and Lee, Mucocutaneous Dyskeratosis Syndromes: A Review, Dermatology and Ophthalmology Reports, 2022
